title: Tenant Network Privacy and Minimal Footprint Specification
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
This document specifies a minimum viable network and hardware footprint for Redwood Inference private deployments where tenant privacy and minimal attack surface are primary constraints. It covers VPC layout recommendations, required and optional telemetry, on‑prem packaging constraints, day‑2 operational guardrails, and a compact upgrade/rollback decision matrix. The goal is to enable field teams and customer infrastructure architects to validate readiness and acceptance criteria for low‑footprint, privacy‑sensitive installs.

Audience
- Field engineers responsible for installs
- Customer infrastructure and security architects
- Product and SRE owners gating minimal SLAs for restricted deployments

Objectives
1) Define a defensible minimum network topology that supports inference runtime and control plane connectivity while minimizing egress and open ports.
2) Provide a short list of hardware constraints for constrained environments (edge racks, branch data closets).
3) Prescribe telemetry that balances observability and data minimization.
4) Give day‑2 runbook primitives and a safe upgrade/rollback matrix with explicit owner actions.

High‑level design principles
- Least privilege by default: only allow the narrowest set of outbound and inbound flows required for runtime and management.
- Auditable telemetry: sampled, redacted, and customer‑scoped.
- Fail‑closed fallbacks: when external control plane connectivity is lost, local inference continues on pinned models; control plane operations are quiesced.
- Immutable packaging: signed images, verified boot where feasible.

1) Network topology (minimal footprint)
Recommended segment layout (logical):
- mgmt-subnet (private): Control plane agent egress to customer control plane endpoints and KMS.
- svc-subnet (private): Model serving runtime nodes (GPU/CPU hosts).
- infra-subnet (private): Basic infra services that must be colocated (NTP, DNS, internal proxy).
- optional-bastion (restricted): Single hardened jump host for field access (only if strictly required).

Minimum IP/Firewall policy (ingress/egress)
- All subnets default deny.
- svc-subnet -> mgmt-subnet: TCP 443 (TLS) to agent endpoint (outbound), TCP 22 only for scheduled maintenance windows if enabled.
- svc-subnet -> KMS: TLS 443 to customer KMS endpoints (only allowed to registered HSM IPs).
- mgmt-subnet -> software‑registry: TLS 443 outbound to pinned registry hostnames/IP ranges (image pulls).
- infra-subnet -> svc-subnet: TCP 123 (NTP), UDP 53 (DNS), TCP 443 if edge proxy used.
- No direct Internet inbound to svc-subnet.

Example iptables-style egress whitelist (illustrative)
- Allow: 10.10.0.0/24:443 -> 172.16.5.10:443 (control-plane agent)
- Allow: svc-subnet:0/0 -> kms.example.corp:443
- Deny: all other outbound except DNS/NTP to infra-resolvers

2) Minimal hardware profile (constrained deployments)
Table: minimum / recommended / notes
- CPU: 8 cores / 16 cores / AVX2 recommended for quantized CPU paths
- RAM: 64GB / 128GB / KV cache and model shards require headroom
- GPU (optional): none / 1x A10 or equivalent / if local accel needed for latency SLOs
- Storage: 1 TB NVMe / 2 TB NVMe / encrypted LUKS or hardware encryption module
- Network: 10 Gbps NIC / 25 Gbps / SR‑IOV optional for shared fabrics

Boot and packaging constraints
- Images must be signed and verified at boot. We provide a signed manifest and an image verification tool.
- Minimal base image: Alpine + runtime agent (containerized) or Ubuntu 22.04 for full‑feature installs.
- Optional air‑gapped packaging: pre‑staged OCI archive and tarball of model artifacts.

3) Telemetry and data minimization policy
Required (low volume, high signal):
- Heartbeats: node ID, version, simple health status (ok/warn/fail), timestamp (1m cadence).
- Aggregated token metrics: token count per model bucket (no PII), hourly rollup.
- Error counters: rate limited and sampled stack traces (1/100) with redaction.

Prohibited:
- No request payload, no input tokens, and no output tokens leave the tenant boundary for privacy‑locked installs.
- No raw KV cache snapshots transmitted.

Telemetry sampling and retention
- Default sampling for detailed traces: 1% (configurable by customer).
- Local retention window for detailed traces: 14 days. Aggregated metrics: 365 days (by default).

4) Day‑2 operations: checklist and quick actions
Critical oncall pages (who to call):
- Field operator primary: oncall-field@redwood.com
- Runtime-engineering escalation: runtime-oncall@redwood.com
- Security escalation: secops@redwood.com

Routine checks (daily):
1) Verify agent heartbeats: expected >= 95% nodes reporting in last 10m.
2) KV cache hit ratio baseline: within 10% of baseline for tenant workload.
3) Disk health: SMART checks and < 80% utilization on NVMe.

Incident primitives (fast paths):
- If control plane connectivity lost but local runtime healthy: change maintenance flag at operator console to prevent automatic upgrades; open ticket with runtime-oncall.
- If a node exhibits repeated OOMs: exclude node from scheduler, collect logs via secure copy (scp to bastion if permitted), and redeploy a fresh image.

Sample commands
- Download and verify a signed image (example):
  curl -sSf https://pinned-registry.example.corp/images/runtime:v1.4.2 --output runtime.tar.gz
  sha256sum -c runtime-v1.4.2.sha256
  ./image-verify runtime.tar.gz runtime.v1.4.2.sig

- Toggle maintenance mode locally:
  # as root on a control node
  systemctl start redwood-maintenance
  redwoodctl maintenance enable --reason "customer isolation window"

5) Compact upgrade and rollback matrix
Principles: prefer incremental, state-preserving upgrades for control plane agents; prefer immutable replacement for runtime nodes. Keep automatic rollback gated by canary metrics and customer approval for privacy‑locked deployments.

Decision matrix (short):
- Patch <= minor security fix (agent only): "Canary -> 24h monitor -> Gradual roll". Auto-rollback if error rate > 2% or heartbeat drop > 10%. Owner: runtime-engineering.
- Runtime binary change affecting KV layout: "Offline migration window -> migration dry run -> customer signoff -> rollout". If migration fails, run documented backout (see Backout steps). Owner: runtime-engineering + customer IT.
- Model format or quantization changes: "Blue/green model swap with mirrored traffic (10% -> 50% -> 100%)". Rollback by demoting traffic routing rules. Owner: product + field operator.

Backout steps (critical)
1) Pause control plane job orchestrator: redwoodctl jobs pause --scope tenant-XYZ
2) Restore pinned image snapshot: redwoodctl node replace --image <old-image> --force-if-healthy
3) Rehydrate KV cache from local snapshot if available: /opt/redwood/kv-backups/restore.sh --from latest
4) Validate: smoke test (sample prompt bank, latency percentile < SLA)

6) Acceptance criteria checklist for customer readiness (go/no‑go)
- Network: firewall policies applied and tested, agent egress only to pinned endpoints.
- Hardware: node provisioning meets the minimal hardware profile.
- Security: image verification and key attestation confirmed.
- Telemetry: minimal telemetry toggled and sampling set to customer preference.
- Failover: service‑level smoke tests pass (5/5 sample prompts within latency target)

7) Security & compliance notes
- Key management: integrate with customer KMS and restrict KMS endpoints by IP and service account. Rotate keys quarterly by default; follow the private deploy KMS rotation runbook for HSM specifics.
- Audit logging: local audit logs retained per customer retention policy and archived to customer‑owned object store if requested.

8) Ownership and escalation matrix
- Installation owner: field-ops@redwood.com (primary)
- Ongoing support owner: runtime-support@redwood.com
- Security owner: secops@redwood.com

Appendix A — Example network policy YAML (Calico-like)
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: GlobalNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: redwood-minimal-egress
spec:
  selector: all()
  egress:
  - action: Allow
    destination:
      nets: ["172.16.5.0/24"] # control plane agents
      ports: [443]
  - action: Allow
    destination:
      nets: ["10.20.0.0/24"] # kms
      ports: [443]
  - action: Allow
    destination:
      selector: "role == 'infra'"
      ports: [53, 123]
  - action: Deny
    destination: 
      nets: ["0.0.0.0/0"]

Appendix B — Minimal smoke test (bash)
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# simple local request to runtime (loopback to avoid egress)
curl -sS -X POST https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer local-test-token' -d '{"model":"small-quant","input":"Hello"}' | jq .

Appendix C — Evidence checklist for handoff
- Signed image manifest and verification output (artifact).
- Network ACL test results (pcap or iptables-save).
- Telemetry config file (redwood-telemetry.yaml) with sampling rates and retention.
- Customer signoff on maintenance window and rollback SLA.
